panels.title: Model call duration, p50/p90/p99, by model
panels.description: Reads duration_ms on kind=model_call Events, the 50th, 90th and 99th percentile duration, one series set per model. Model calls are sparse relative to $__interval, so null buckets are bridged (spanNulls) and every point is drawn, turning what would otherwise be isolated dots into a readable line.

panels.title: Model call duration, overall distribution
panels.description: Reads duration_ms on kind=model_call Events, the median duration per Session, one value per session_id. Loki cannot histogram a raw per-call value because duration_ms is unwrapped rather than a label, so this is the per-Session distribution, the same limitation the Sessions dashboard notes for its wall-time histogram.

targets.expr: quantile_over_time(0.5, {service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="model_call" | unwrap duration_ms [$__range]) by (session_id)

panels.title: Maximum model call duration in range
panels.description: Reads duration_ms on kind=model_call Events, the maximum value anywhere in the selected range, coloured by thresholds at 10s and 30s.

targets.expr: max(max_over_time({service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="model_call" | unwrap duration_ms [$__range]))

panels.title: Slowest 50 model calls
panels.description: Reads kind=model_call Events as raw log lines, a range query over the selected range. A label_format stage shortens session_id to 8 characters before the Extract fields transformation splits the raw labels field into one field per Event attribute, convertFieldType makes duration_ms, input_tokens and output_tokens numeric so duration_ms sorts correctly, and the table is sorted by duration_ms descending and limited to the slowest 50. Columns: the call Time, model, Duration (ms, millisecond-unit override), Session, input tokens and output tokens; every other Event attribute and log field the unprocessed logs query would otherwise show is dropped.

targets.expr: {service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="model_call" | label_format session_id="{{ .session_id | trunc 8 }}"

panels.title: Duration against output tokens
panels.description: Reads duration_ms and output_tokens on kind=model_call Events as raw log lines, a range query, skipping an Event missing either field. Extract fields splits the raw labels field, convertFieldType makes both fields numeric, Organize fields reduces the frame to exactly those two numeric fields with output_tokens first, and sortBy orders the rows by output_tokens ascending. Drawn as a `trend` panel, not `xychart`: the xychart plugin does not load in this Grafana image. The trend panel reads output_tokens as its x axis, points only (no connecting line), against duration_ms on the y axis.

targets.expr: {service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="model_call" | output_tokens != "" | duration_ms != ""

panels.title: Duration against input tokens
panels.description: Reads duration_ms and input_tokens on kind=model_call Events as raw log lines, a range query, skipping an Event missing either field. Extract fields splits the raw labels field, convertFieldType makes both fields numeric. Unlike its output_tokens sibling, input_tokens takes only a handful of distinct values across hundreds of Events, so a raw per-row frame has long runs of a repeated x value; a trend panel demands a unique, ascending x field, so groupBy first collapses the duplicate input_tokens rows into one row per distinct value, averaging duration_ms. Organize fields renames the averaged column back to duration_ms and reduces the frame to exactly those two numeric fields with input_tokens first, and sortBy then orders the now-unique rows by input_tokens ascending. Drawn as a `trend` panel, not `xychart`: the xychart plugin does not load in this Grafana image. The trend panel reads input_tokens as its x axis, points only (no connecting line), against mean duration_ms on the y axis.

targets.expr: {service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="model_call" | input_tokens != "" | duration_ms != ""

panels.title: Output tokens per second, by model
panels.description: Reads output_tokens and duration_ms on kind=model_call Events, the summed output_tokens divided by the summed duration_ms (scaled from milliseconds to seconds) in each interval, one series per model.

targets.expr: sum by (model) (sum_over_time({service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="model_call" | unwrap output_tokens [$__interval])) / (sum by (model) (sum_over_time({service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="model_call" | unwrap duration_ms [$__interval])) / 1000)

panels.title: Model call duration over time, by Session
panels.description: Reads duration_ms on kind=model_call Events, the maximum value in each interval, one series per session_id. label_format shortens session_id to its first 8 characters before grouping, so the legend reads a short id rather than the full 36-character Session identifier, and the legend sits in a table to the right rather than a wide bottom list. Model calls are sparse relative to $__interval, so null buckets are bridged (spanNulls) and every point is drawn, turning what would otherwise be isolated dots into a readable line.

targets.expr: max by (session_id) (max_over_time({service_name=~".+", agent=~"$agent", project=~"$project", session_id=~"$session_id", run_id=~"$run_id", task=~"$task", variant=~"$variant"} | kind="model_call" | label_format session_id="{{ trunc 8 .session_id }}" | unwrap duration_ms [$__interval]))

panels.description: Reads mcp_server.internal_ms and mcp_server.upstream_ms on kind=mcp_server_call Events, both SHOULD attributes, summed per interval and stacked, so the split between a server's own work and its upstream wait is visible. Only 184 mcp_server_call Events exist, so this panel can return no data outside a narrow range.
